tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on user-facing symptoms and intents (answers worse, hallucinating, responses cut off, comparing models, LLMOps maturity) rather than implementation details, explicitly lists trigger contexts including cases where the user doesn't name the domain directly ('even if they do not mention evaluation jobs...by name'), and is concise (a short paragraph).
tests.evidence: Use this skill when answers have got worse or a model may be hallucinating more, when responses are being cut off, when nobody can say whether quality regressed, when an evaluation job fails, or when someone asks how to compare two models or how mature their LLMOps practice is, even if they do not mention evaluation jobs, regression gates, promotion criteria or finish reasons by name.

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is dense but every section conveys domain-specific, non-obvious information (check-ids, read-only API boundaries, finish-reason mechanics, routing rules) rather than explaining concepts the agent already knows. There is no generic explanation of what evaluation or CloudWatch is.
tests.evidence: 'Together these back three checks: LLM-EVAL-012 (the shift itself), LLM-EVAL-013 (no metric filter...), and LLM-EVAL-014 (OutputTokenCount rising with flat Invocations...)' — this is project-specific, not generic explanation.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (read-only API enforcement, finish-reason measurement, delegation payload columns) are highly prescriptive, while synthesis and prioritization steps allow agent judgment with explained rationale.
tests.evidence: 'Read-only. Never call a mutating API. Recommend the fix; never apply it.' is prescriptive for a fragile/dangerous operation, while 'For an incident, lead with the root cause... and the highest-impact action' gives flexible guidance for synthesis.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The skill consistently designates a default first read/action per scenario in the Router table rather than listing multiple equal options.
tests.evidence: 'Do we have evals, is quality measured at all | `ListEvaluationJobs` (confirm regional support first) | ...' shows one clear default call per row.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable investigation procedure (5 steps) and routing rules applicable to any evaluation question, not a one-off task declaration.
tests.evidence: 'Step 1: Understand the question and establish scope... Step 2: Collect evaluation state... Step 3: Evaluate against the check catalog...' generalizes across any evaluation-related request.
